feature-prd.name: platform-foundation
feature-prd.overview: The cross-cutting platform layer that every persona WO sits on top of: shared data model, authentication, per-city configuration, dedup engine, status trail, push notifications, audit log, polling infrastructure, i18n framework. Produces APIs + data models; consumes no UI.

requirement.name: data-model
requirement.description: Single shared `Ticket` entity + per-city config entities, enforced in PostgreSQL via Prisma. Internal-only fields are hidden from citizen queries via API layer (not via DB row-level security in v1 — simpler and adequate for the pilot).

acceptance.criterion: Single `Ticket` entity with fields: id, city_id, category_id, ward_id, reporter_id, assigned_crew_id, status, photo_urls (ordered JSONB array), location (lat/lng + reverse-geocoded label), note, created_at, status_trail (JSONB array of {status, actor_id, timestamp, note?})
Status enum: submitted → routed → in_progress → resolved. Closed/cancelled is terminal.
Per-city config entities: City, Ward (with GeoJSON polygon), Category, Department, Language
Internal-only fields (assigned_crew_id, internal notes, before-photos from Rashid's perspective) hidden from citizen queries via API layer
Prisma migration runs cleanly against an empty Postgres; seed script creates Dhaka city + template categories

requirement.verification: - npx prisma migrate dev runs cleanly - npm run db:seed creates the Dhaka fixture - Unit test: GET /api/tickets/:id as citizen does NOT include assigned_crew_id - Unit test: GET /api/tickets/:id as dispatcher DOES include assigned_crew_id

requirement.name: auth-roles
requirement.description: Four-role model (citizen / dispatcher / crew / admin). HTTP-only signed session cookies. Argon2 password hashing. WebAuthn mandatory for admin writes. Citizen OTP via SMS (provider abstraction; concrete provider chosen in WO-004).

acceptance.criterion: Four roles enforced at the API layer; no custom-role builder in v1
Citizen registration: phone (unique per city), NID (validated format), name, password (min-length policy), OTP verification
OTP: SMS-based, ≤ 5 min TTL, single-use, retry-cap documented
WebAuthn mandatory for any admin write action; optional for dispatcher/crew in v1
Dispatcher + crew sessions bind to (city, ward, department); cross-scope queries denied at API layer
Argon2 password hashing (via @node-rs/argon2)
@simplewebauthn/server + /browser for WebAuthn
HTTP-only SameSite=Lax Secure signed session cookies

requirement.verification: - Integration test: citizen can register, verify OTP, log in, see their own tickets only - Integration test: dispatcher session bound to ward X cannot read tickets from ward Y - Integration test: admin write action without WebAuthn is rejected - Unit test: argon2 hash verification round-trip

requirement.name: per-city-config
requirement.description: City is a first-class entity. Every ticket, user, category, ward belongs to a city. Dhaka template pre-populates categories, departments, ward template, language defaults.

acceptance.criterion: `City` is first-class; foreign keys cascade-restrict (never delete a city with tickets)
Dhaka template seeds: 5 categories (streetlight, pothole, drainage, garbage, other), 3 departments, 50 wards template, Bangla default
Per-user language override allowed; falls back to city default
Ward polygons stored as GeoJSON; served from GET /api/cities/:id/wards

requirement.verification: - Integration test: POST /api/cities creates a city from Dhaka template - Integration test: GET /api/cities/:id/wards returns the ward list with valid GeoJSON - Unit test: per-user language preference overrides city default

requirement.name: dedup-engine
requirement.description: When a new report is submitted within X meters of an existing open ticket of the same category, the API returns the existing ticket and a `dedup_match: true` flag instead of creating a duplicate. Dedup is a **prompt**, not auto-merge (Feature #3 design rationale).

acceptance.criterion: POST /api/tickets with location within X meters of same-category open ticket returns {dedup_match: true, existing_ticket: {...}} instead of creating new
Dedup radius default = 50m (configurable per city via Aamir; pinned in PRD)
Every dedup attempt logged to audit log (actor, both ticket IDs, distance, category, accepted/rejected)

requirement.verification: - Integration test: two POSTs to /api/tickets at same location within 50m → second returns dedup_match - Integration test: two POSTs at 100m distance → second creates new ticket - Unit test: audit log entry created on every dedup attempt

deferred-to-prd.item: Specific OTP SMS provider (provider abstraction; chosen in WO-004)

requirement.name: status-trail
requirement.description: Every status transition records {from_status, to_status, actor_id, timestamp, optional note} on the ticket. Citizen query returns trail with internal actors anonymized.

acceptance.criterion: Every transition appends a trail entry atomically with the status change
Citizen-facing serializer maps actor_id to "City corporation" (anonymized)
Dispatcher/crew/admin serializers expose the actual actor
Status transitions are atomic (single Postgres transaction)

requirement.verification: - Integration test: POST /api/tickets/:id/transition writes trail entry - Unit test: citizen-facing serializer omits actor_id detail - Unit test: invalid transition (e.g., submitted → resolved skipping routed) returns 409

requirement.name: push-notifications
requirement.description: Per WO-000 acceptance criteria + tech-audit §3: Web Push API (VAPID) transport. Service-worker delivery. Subscribed per-citizen per-their- own-tickets (privacy). UI consumption (when subscribed) lives in WO-001 and WO-002.

acceptance.criterion: POST /api/v1/push/subscribe accepts a citizen's Web Push subscription; stored per (citizen_id, ticket_id scope)
On every status transition, the platform sends push to all subscribed citizens for that ticket
At-least-once delivery with idempotency token (status transition timestamp + ticket_id)
DELETE /api/v1/push/subscribe removes subscription
VAPID keys generated at deploy time and stored as env vars (PUBLIC_VAPID_KEY, PRIVATE_VAPID_KEY)

requirement.verification: - Integration test: subscription persisted; transition triggers push - Unit test: idempotency token prevents duplicate sends on retry
requirement.deferred: FCM (Android native) and APNs (iOS native) — deferred until native wrappers ship

requirement.name: audit-log
requirement.description: Every ticket transition and every per-city config change is written to an append-only audit log. Records: {entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, before_value, after_value, timestamp}.

acceptance.criterion: Append-only AuditEntry table; no UPDATE/DELETE allowed at the API layer
GET /api/audit?entity_type=ticket&entity_id=X returns paginated audit entries (admin-only)
Audit records include before/after JSON snapshots of the changed fields

requirement.verification: - Integration test: ticket transition writes audit entry with before/after - Integration test: per-city config update (e.g., category rename) writes audit entry - Unit test: DELETE on audit row is rejected

requirement.name: polling-infrastructure
requirement.description: Clients poll every 10-30s for status changes. WebSocket deferred to v1.1. Polling rate-limited per actor and per ticket.

acceptance.criterion: GET /api/tickets/:id returns {ticket, trail, last_poll_cursor}
GET /api/tickets?city_id=X&updated_since=cursor returns tickets updated since cursor
Polling rate-limited: max 1 req/sec per (actor_id, ticket_id); 429 with retry-after on overflow

requirement.verification: - Integration test: 2 rapid GETs within 1s to /api/tickets/:id → second is 429 - Integration test: last_poll_cursor updates correctly across polls

requirement.name: i18n
requirement.description: Bangla-first, English-secondary. Per-user language preference stored on the user; falls back to city default.

acceptance.criterion: Translation key registry at /lib/i18n/keys.ts (typed, tree-shakeable)
Per-user language override; falls back to city default; falls back to English
Server-side rendering uses Accept-Language header as the seed when no user preference exists
Bangla is default for Dhaka city; English secondary

requirement.verification: - Unit test: t('home.greeting', 'bn') returns Bangla string - Unit test: user override beats city default beats English fallback

do-not-change.item: Four-role model (citizen / dispatcher / crew / admin); no custom-role builder in v1
WebAuthn mandatory for admin writes (Phase 1 lock)
Dedup is a prompt, not auto-merge (Feature #3 design rationale)
Internal-fields-hidden-from-citizens boundary on every schema addition
Polling (10–30s) for v1; WebSocket deferred to v1.1

performance.item: POST /api/tickets returns in ≤ 300 ms p95 (without photo upload)

security.item: Rate limiting on auth endpoints (OTP, login) to prevent brute force

out-of-scope.item: Any UI page (the platform layer is API + data only)
Map rendering — MapLibre integration lands in WO-001 / WO-002
File-upload UX — lands in WO-001 (citizen photo) and WO-003 (before/after)
Push subscription UI prompt — lands in WO-001
Aamir's provisioning UI — lands in WO-004
Map tile provider configuration — lands in WO-001 (dev uses OSM, prod-if-load-justifies)
